raw_recipe.headline: Creamy Horseradish Garlic Spread
raw_recipe.description: Perfect for fresh veggies, to serve with meats, or just to put on a cracker, this quick sour cream spread adds the flavors of horseradish, garlic, dill, and pepper.
raw_recipe.name: Creamy Horseradish Garlic Spread

recipeInstructions.text: Mix together the sour cream, mayonnaise, horseradish, garlic, salt, black and white pepper, dill, and garlic powder in a bowl. Chill in the refrigerator for at least 20 minutes before serving.

review.reviewBody: In a word, FABULOUS! I've tried other horseradish dipping sauces on this site and this is by far the best! I would liken this more to of a spread/dip simply because it's just so versatile. I used reduced fat sour cream and Hellman's light mayo and this was oh so good! What's great about this is you can customize this to your tastes by adjusting the amounts of horseradish, garlic and dill - but no matter what you do it's bound to be delicious. I made this as a topping for some juicy burgers. I used the leftovers for some cut up veggies and my husband's sandwich for work. I can't wait to try this as on grilled steak sandwiches! Thanks for the great recipe ADZELL!

More a sauce than a spread, this blew everyone away at the dinner table tonight. My gosh this was good! I knew it was gonna be awesome right after I made it but of course it only got better after the flavors developed after several hours in the fridge. I might have used a little less pepper than called for since the horseradish I used really had a bite, but other than that I made no other changes, tho' I admit I didn't measure precisely. I served this with our corned beef and cabbage dinner, but I sure woudn't limit it to just that! This would also go well with prime rib, roast beef sandwiches, a dip for vegetables and quite possibly even on potatoes. We all SO enjoyed this that the bowl was scraped clean. A truly unforgettable sauce/spread.

We really enjoy this spread/dip slathered on the base of the buns of our French beef dips. I purchase fresh bakery sub/hoagie rolls. Pile on tender roast beef slices, sauteed green, yellow, red peppers strips, caramelized onions, provolone cheese slices (or your preferred) melted while quickly broiled in the oven (watch constantly & carefully!) or toast in an air fryer basket a minute or 2. Serve with a side of beef au jus for dipping. I take a shortcut and buy a packaged mix. SO tasty. I enjoy this spread a lot and appreciate all the other creative ideas. I've had people wonder why my roast beef french dips taste so good. It's also adaptable, so if you like more or less horseradish, dill taste, pepper, salt, etc., then adapt it, but I tend to try as is first, then taste. I think this is now a must and I suggest if you have time, make it earlier or a day before to let the flavours meld covered in a bowl or in a mason jar in the fridge. Excellent, but it's still tasty same day. Thanks for posting. It's in my rotation now. PS: I have a very fussy family guest who is afraid of horseradish, but gobbled the offering and still requests without knowing it that the creamy, jarred spoonful forms part of the subtle flavor. I have another who adds another tablespoon of creamy jarred horseradish to their bun. Do your own thing to your taste!

The big guy and I loved this sauce. The only change I made was to increase the amount of horseradish to our taste, we love horseradish so I increased the amount by 2.5 times. The sauce was refrigerated for over 4 hours before using and that allowed the garlic and herbs to infuse thoroughly. This was excellent on our St Patrick's Day corned beef brisket. It would also be amazing on roast beef, fish or shrimp. Super simple to make and uses simple ingredients.

I loved this sauce!! I used 1/2 and 1/2 sour cream and plain yogurt, doubled the dill and doubled the horseradish. I will make this again! The consistency made it a terrific spread, add a couple drops of milk and it would be a stellar dip.

I made this recipe exactly as written, EXCEPT...I substituted 4oz cream cheese for the sour cream. I needed something to bring to a party, and as I went a little overboard with the buy-one-get one free deli roast beef the other day, I was trying to think of a way to use some of it up. I thought the flavors in this recipe would also make a good cheese spread so I tried it. It was awesome!!! I let the flavors mellow overnight in the fridge, then spread the mixture on some original flavored melba toasts. I topped each with a folded slice of deli roast beef, sprinkled a pinch of grated parmesan cheese and a few fresh chives on top to make them pretty, and put them on a platter. They were absolutely delicious - mine was the only empty plate at the end of the night. The balance of flavors is delicate and just right. Thank you so much for sharing this recipe! Can't wait to try the sour cream version with beef tenderloin.

**EDIT: I made this again and I had to change my rating to 5 stars. This is really, really good on sandwiches made with leftover roast beef!! I'll be making this again and again! Thank you! ** EDIT**



Just ok as far as my tastes but I gave it a 4 star rating as my son really enjoyed it. I doubled the horseradish and garlic, used a full tsp of the dill.

Delicious! I'll be letting it sit for a day or so to let the flavors blend. I did sub plain non-fat Greek yogurt for the the sour cream, which I do frequently. It was a bit tart so I also added a tsp or so of white sugar which helped cut the tang. I look forward to using this as a sandwich spread, a veggie dip, or with meats. Thanks for a great recipe, ADZELL!

This was a hit in our house. By mistake, I added 2 tablespoons of Grey Poupon Harvest coarse ground mustard. I did compensate by adding in 2 1/2 tablespoons of horseradish. I also used miracle whip instead of mayonnaise as this was in the refrigerator. I will try this again both ways.
Wonderful sauce. I always double the recipe as it's great on baked potatoes, steak and sandwiches!

LOVED THIS! As another reviewer did, I served this with Corned Beef and Cabbage dinner (by LUSYRSGIRL). It was a huge hit! This could be used for anything! I did not have white pepper so omitted that. I had fresh dill not dry so microwaved that in paper towels at 50% power for a minute and used that cut up. I also doubled the recipe. Will be making this again and again! Thank you!!!!!

This is it, folks. You're new favorite spread/dip. I made it with no changes, and it had a perfectly balanced flavor profile. You can use this on just about any meat or sandwhich. Veggies too. It's so quick and easy! Make it the night before, and thank yourself the next day. The best part about this recipe is that it is customizable. You can thin it out with a little milk, or you can play around with the amounts of the seasonings to suit your taste, or your dish.

Made this for Christmas with make-your-own beef tenderloin sliders. The spread was easy to make--had all the ingredients in the fridge. I did add a little more horseradish as we like it with a "little bite".
Thanks for recipe!
This spread/dip is really good and addictive. My husband loved it. As other's have said it works good as a spread for beef sandwiches or a dip for steaks , veggies, and crackers. Yummy!
Excellent and exactly what I was looking for to top the crock pot Italian beef sandwiches from this site. Thank you!

Absolutely delicious! It brought my whole corned beef meal up 10 notches. Made it exactly as described, though I doubled it . Because of the rave reviews, I am going to use it on my salmon tonight, then on my corned beef reubens tomorrow. I have a feeling my loved ones are going to ask for this repeatedly!

Used this spread over corned beef last night for St Patrick's Day meal. The spread was extraordinarily good. Will use it as a "go-to" for many other meats - like steak, Thanksgiving beef tenderloin, chicken, pork tenderloin, etc. This beats straight horseradish all to h.....!
I followed the recipe exactly. I'll add more horseradish, garlic and dill, which is why the 4 stars. But it is excellent. I've been eating it all week :)
This dip is quick and easy to make, it was devoured by my guests! Perfect with corned beef but could be used with any sandwich too.
As suggested, I made it "to taste"....adding more horseradish. Great recipe from A2!
